MULTIPLICATION of Matrices and SCALAR:
 The product of two matrices, A and B, results in a third matrix C. Each element of C, denoted as Cij, is the sum of the products of the corresponding elements of the ith row of A and the jth column of B.
 It's important to note that the number of columns in A must equal the number of rows in B to perform multiplication.

Let A = [a11 a12]
 [a21 a22]
And B = [b11 b12]
 [b21 b22]

Then, the product AB is:
 AB = [ (a11*b11 + a12*b21) (a11*b12 + a12*b22) ]
 [ (a21*b11 + a22*b21) (a21*b12 + a22*b22) ]

 We also have scalar mutiplication which refers to the multiplication of each term of a matrix with a scalar term.
 If a scalar let’s have ‘k’ is multiplied by a matrix then the equivalent matrix will contain elements equal to the product of the scalar and the element of the original matrix.
